Subject: RE: [ALERT] Newbridge - burst throughput drop (US-west)

Quick telemetry summary after initial triage:
- Kernel rollouts: none this morning for the us-west fleet; last change was 09/28 (no correlation).
- Autoscaler: observed a short suppression window between 08:42–08:51 where scaling decisions delayed due to noisy CPU signals; control-plane logs attached in newbridge-error-logs.zip (controlplane-logs.txt).
- KV cache: shard 4 shows elevated eviction rate (4.8x usual) at 08:44 coincident with a client-side retry storm. Cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 63% for several minutes.
- Immediate mitigation executed (09:20): forced warm-up script on affected nodes, temporarily raised cache size for shard 4 and disabled aggressive eviction policy. Early signals: error rate down to ~1.6%, P95 latency trending toward 180ms.

Next steps I recommend now:
1) Keep the cache size raised for 2 hours and monitor real traffic for regressions. (Owner: David)
2) Roll a targeted config rollback for autoscaler suppression heuristics (small risk) and observe for 30m. (Owner: Karthik)
3) Prepare a short exec summary that includes: impact window, mitigations performed, and residual risk. (Owner: Priyom / Marissa)

I'll stay in the war-room and update every 30 minutes.

— David
VP, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Our engineers applied a targeted cache warm-up and raised the cache allocation for the affected shard at ~09:20 PT and are monitoring. Early indicators show error rates falling from ~4.2% to ~1.6% and P95 latency moving back toward baseline.

What we are committing to now:
- Hourly status updates until the window closes (next update at 11:15 PT).

- If there is customer-visible regression in the next 90 minutes, we will open a direct bridge with your SREs.

If you need an immediate call, I can host the bridge now.
